sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the Petitioners and learned counsel for the State.

2. The Petitioners are accused in connection with G.R. Case No.44 of 2022 pending on the file of learned J.M.F.C. (Rural) Sundargarh arising out of Dhuruadihi P.S. Case No.163 of 2022 for commission of offence alleged under Sections 420/468/471/120-B of IPC.
3. Learned counsel, on instruction, submits that except the present BLAPL, no other bail application of the Petitioners relating to the aforementioned P.S. case is pending in any other Court.

4. Being aggrieved by the rejection of their application for bail U/s.483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) by the learned Sessions Judge, Sundargarh by order dated 17.09.2024 in the aforementioned cases, the present BLAPL has been filed.

5. It is submitted that in the case at hand the allegation against the Petitioners is that they lured the informant to part with a sum of Rs.25,00,000/- (Rupees Twenty-Five Lakhs) on the pretext of selling him ancient gold and magic coin.

6. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the Petitioners that the principal accused, namely,
Sunny Kumar has since been released on default bail and as such, further continuance of the Petitioners in custody is not warranted.

sentences.text:
It is his further submission that it is highly improbable that the entire amount, as claimed, has been paid in cash and it is stated that taking into account the nature of allegation, Petitioners may be released on bail.
8.

Learned counsel for the State opposes the prayer for bail and submits that on the basis of statements of the witnesses, statements recorded U/s.161 Cr.P.C. as well as the verification of bank account, it comes to the fore that a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- (Rupees Three Lakhs) has been credited to the account of the Petitioner No.1 (Dasaratha Soreng).
9.
It is his further submission that all the Petitioners have criminal antecedent of the similar nature.
10. Learned counsel submits that the Petitioners are on bail in such cases.

11. During the course of submission, learned counsel for the Petitioners, on instruction, submits that without prejudice to the rights and contentions of the parties, Petitioners are prepared to pay a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- (Rupees Three Lakhs) out of which Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand) shall be paid as a condition precedent for release and thereafter, the balance of Rs.2,50,000/- (Rupees Two Lakhs Fifty Thousand) shall be paid in five equal installments.
The first of which shall fall due after one month of such release.
A memo to the said effect filed in Court is taken on record.

12. Considering the nature of allegations, the filing of the charge sheet and the undertaking, as noted, this Court directs the Petitioners to be released on bail on such terms to be fixed by the learned Court in seisin.

13. Before releasing, the Petitioners shall deposit Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand), as undertaken and the balance of Rs.2,50,000/- (Rupees Two Lakhs Fifty Thousand) shall be paid in five equal installments, the first of which shall fall due after one month of such release, which shall be fixed by the learned Court in seisin.
14.
The amount, as deposited, shall be kept in an interest bearing account which shall abide by the final outcome of the case at hand.
However, it shall be open to the Complainant to seek release in accordance with law.
15. In case of any default in the matter of payment of monthly installments, as directed, it shall be open for the learned Court in seisin to take necessary action in accordance with law.

16. It is needless to state here that the observations made herein are only for the purpose of consideration of this bail application and the direction to deposit, on the basis of undertaking as noted, ought not to be constructed as this Court expressing any view regarding the complicity of the Petitioners which has to be established in an independent manner in the ongoing trial on the basis of materials on record.
17. Accordingly, the BLAPL stands disposed of.
